title: Enigmatic cluster targeted by Hubble
caption: The globular cluster NGC 6401, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: NGC 6401 · constellation Ophiuchus · about 35000 light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: ESA/Hubble Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: Hubble's sharp optics break the globular cluster NGC 6401 into its individual stars. Through older telescopes it looked like a ghostly mist. The cluster lies in Ophiuchus, the Serpent Bearer, and is faint enough that seeing it takes a telescope and some experience.

Globular clusters are rich, generally spherical groups of stars that orbit the cores of galaxies, bound together by gravity. The Milky Way has around 160, and they contain some of the oldest stars known. Their origin and role in how galaxies evolve are still not fully understood.

NGC 6401 has fooled observers before. William Herschel discovered it in 1784 but thought it was a bright nebula, and his son John made the same mistake. In 1977 astronomers thought they had found a planetary nebula in it, but a 1990 study concluded the object is a symbiotic star: a red giant paired with a small hot star, wrapped in nebulosity.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (3.29 x 1.50 arcminutes) and distance (35000 light years), the frame spans roughly 33 × 15 light-years. Its light set out about 35,000 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This image uses the Wide Field Channel of Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys: a yellow-orange filter (F606W) is shown in blue and a near-infrared filter (F814W) in red.
understand.eye: Where early observers saw a misty patch, Hubble resolves separate stars, and part of the data is near-infrared light invisible to the eye.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.
behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

explore: Because symbiotic stars are thought to turn into a kind of planetary nebula in time, the 1977 claim may simply have been early. Exposure times were 680 and 580 seconds, and the field of view is 3.3 by 1.5 arcminutes.
alt: A globular cluster resolved into many individual stars.
